card.shortVersion: Real chef Marcus Wareing taught actors to cook for the film.
card.longDescription: Real-life chef Marcus Wareing was recruited to advise the actors and provide input on the script for "Burnt." His consultancy included teaching the core actors to cook and act like chefs, alongside kitchen and food design. The film's kitchen set was constructed as a fully functioning kitchen, designed to operate like a real restaurant. Sienna Miller, who plays sous chef Helene, dedicated extra time to learn cooking, aiming to be a cook rather than merely acting like one.

card.shortVersion: Bradley Cooper trained to act and cook like a real chef.
card.longDescription: To prepare for his role as Adam Jones, Bradley Cooper and other core actors were taught to cook and act like professional chefs by consultant Marcus Wareing. Wareing observed that top actors like Cooper could embody the role, even learning to wear chef whites authentically. Cooper already possessed some cooking experience, which helped him portray the aggressive chef. Furthermore, all food preparation scenes in the movie were filmed with actual cooking to ensure realism.

card.shortVersion: The kitchen set was fully functional, and actors cooked for real.
card.longDescription: The film's kitchen set was a fully functional environment, built to operate like a real restaurant kitchen. Consultant chef Marcus Wareing ensured a strong and realistic atmosphere, even turning the stoves on full to make the actors genuinely hot and sweaty. Sienna Miller, playing Helene, performed her own cooking, expertly preparing multiple fish dishes simultaneously. The demanding conditions led to Miller frequently getting cut and burned during filming.
